intro: Executive assistants manage calendars, people and priorities for senior leaders, which makes them strong candidates for management. The closest of the 25 careers below is Administrative Services Managers, with a 90% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $114,130, which is 49% more than the $76,590 executive assistants earn.
why_it_works: Your day is anticipating what an executive needs, handling sensitive information and keeping many people coordinated. O*NET rates service orientation at 3.75 out of 5 for this job, and coordination at 3.38. Office management, HR and project roles use the same organizing skills. About half of the matches need a bachelor's degree. The gaps are managing people and budgets.
tips: Ask to own a budget or lead an office project; both are proof for administrative services manager roles.
Project Management Specialists earn $102,320, which is 34% more, and a certificate can help.
Paralegals are a 79% match if you want detailed legal work, though pay is lower at $62,890.

faq.q: What jobs can former executive assistants do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Administrative Services Managers (90%), office and administrative supervisors (90%) and Human Resources Specialists (82%), based on O*NET 31.0. Project Management Specialists are 78% matched and earn $102,320, which is 34% more than the $76,590 executive assistant median.

faq.q: Which careers for executive assistants pay more?
faq.a: 12 of the 25 matches pay more. Financial Managers earn $166,570 (117% more), Public Relations Managers $146,910 (92% more) and Fundraising Managers $125,470 (64% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. These manager roles usually need a bachelor's degree and experience.

faq.q: Do executive assistants need a degree to move up?
faq.a: For about half of the paths. 12 of the 25 matches need no more education than executive assistants already have, including 8 of the top 10. A bachelor's degree is common in close matches, held by 45% of workers in one of them.

faq.q: What skills should executive assistants build?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are managing people, operations analysis, managing financial resources and troubleshooting. Time management already rates 3.25 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so supervising staff and handling budgets are the main steps toward manager roles.
